clue.text: Hitting the monarch with a turned-up nose

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the slang word for nose is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: conk is British slang for a nose
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: Someone is striking a haughty, snub-nosed king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned-up' turns CONK into KNOC; the snub-nose picture hides the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Knocking is striking or rapping, a synonym of hitting.

clue.text: Bruised son of Aphrodite northward goes

indicators.note: in a down clue, going northward means the god's name is written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Eros, the Greek god of love, is the son of Aphrodite

explanation.surface: Cupid's Greek counterpart heads north nursing his bruises.
explanation.definitionFit: A sore spot is a bruised, tender one, so the adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: I'm taking yonks such figures to provide

parts.note: the apostrophe dropped, I'm gives the letters IM
yonks is British slang for a very long time, like ages

explanation.surface: A painter says it will take forever to supply such pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: YONKS is British informal for a very long time.
explanation.definitionFit: Images are figures in the sense of pictures, statues or likenesses.

clue.text: Valuable hints most females try to hide

definitions.meaning: a wrinkle is an informal word for a useful tip or clever dodge
creases in the skin that come with age, which many women conceal

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a handy tip and a crease of ageing skin, the two senses here.

clue.text: Steady! Unsteady rider needs a fling

indicators.note: something unsteady wobbles out of place, so the letters of the next words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wobbly horseman is told to calm down and go for a brief affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unsteady' shuffles RIDER and FLING; 'Steady!' reads as a command but is the noun, an informal word for a regular partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A steady is an informal term for a regular romantic partner.

clue.text: Sit up and beg and dry eyes I may bring

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word sit is written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to sue is to beg or plead, as in suing for peace

explanation.surface: A dog is told to sit up and beg, and something offers to dry its tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sit up and beg' reads as a dog trick; 'up' works on 'Sit' alone, since this is a down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper handkerchief is used to wipe away tears, which is what the clue describes.

clue.text: Trendy at first, his news he must recall

parts.note: in means fashionable or trendy
former means earlier, what came at first

explanation.surface: A fashionable man must remember his news from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A police source or grass reports what he knows, recounting news to the authorities.

clue.text: Too red to change, being inveterate

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are made to change their order

explanation.surface: Someone is too red-faced to alter their deeply set habits.
explanation.definitionFit: Rooted and inveterate both describe something deeply established and long ingrained.

clue.text: Fruit lasts in "what into each life must fall"

indicators.note: the shorter piece sits inside the quoted saying's word

parts.note: the proverb says into each life some rain must fall
lasts means continues to be, so it gives is

explanation.surface: A dried fruit quotes Longfellow's line about rain.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation is Longfellow's 'Into each life some rain must fall'.
explanation.definitionFit: A raisin is a dried grape, a kind of fruit.

clue.text: The suffering a preacher tries to hide

indicators.note: the letters sit concealed within the words a preacher

explanation.surface: A preacher tries to conceal his suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tries to hide' shows the answer is inside 'a preacher'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache is a continuous pain, a form of suffering.

clue.text: Earth getting smaller? That's unjustified!

parts.note: ground is earth or soil
less means smaller in amount

explanation.surface: Someone protests that the claim the planet is shrinking has no basis.
explanation.definitionFit: Something groundless has no basis, so it is unjustified.

clue.text: Titles, perhaps mysteries, so they say

indicators.note: so they say signals a word said out loud sounding like another

parts.note: rites are religious mysteries or ceremonies

explanation.surface: Someone speculates about titles to secret ceremonies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so they say' means a sound-alike: RITES sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Titles to property are legal entitlements, examples of what people hold by law.

clue.text: Shaw's house must have the will to separate

parts.note: heart means will or spirit, as in having the heart to do something
to break is to separate into pieces

explanation.surface: George Bernard Shaw's household must have the determination to split up.
explanation.walkthrough: Shaw wrote the play Heartbreak House, so the definition takes the word in front of House.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw's play is titled Heartbreak House, so this word names his house.

clue.text: Makes greater generals in a proper way

indicators.note: the letters of the word generals are put into a proper new order

explanation.surface: Proper procedure is promoting generals to higher rank.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlarge is to make bigger, a synonym of making greater.

clue.text: A cricket stroke — this cursory look could tell

definitions.meaning: a batting stroke deflecting the ball fine off the bat face

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a deflecting cricket shot and a brief look.

clue.text: Shy and remote, he must have been unshipped

parts.note: to shy is to throw, and to cast is also to throw
away means distant or remote

explanation.surface: A shy, distant man must once have been put off a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shy' looks like the timid adjective but is the verb to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: A castaway is someone shipwrecked or marooned, put ashore off a vessel.

clue.text: The shaken sorbet makes this man still well!

indicators.note: a sorbet that has been shaken has its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: A shaken-up sorbet still produces a healthy man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaken' rearranges SORBET. The definition plays on Sit-well: 'still' is SIT, so the man is the writer Osbert Sitwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Osbert Sitwell was an English writer; still and well spell out his surname in parts.

clue.text: Composer's old love by a number gripped

indicators.note: the number holds the archaic word for a lover inside it

parts.note: ten is a number
leman is an archaic word for a lover or sweetheart

explanation.surface: A composer's former sweetheart is held by a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: LEMAN is an old word for a sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: Georg Philipp Telemann was a German Baroque composer.

clue.text: More angry, "upstairs, downstairs". So to speak

indicators.note: in a down clue, the word reads the same going up as coming down

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: An angrier person is described as going upstairs and downstairs.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is a palindrome: in a down light it reads the same upwards and downwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Redder describes a face more flushed with anger, so it means more angry.

clue.text: Aversion shows how Sid reverts to style

indicators.note: reverts means the name Sid is turned back to front

parts.note: taste is style or discernment

explanation.surface: A man named Sid goes back to old habits and shows his dislike.
explanation.definitionFit: Distaste is a feeling of dislike, the same as aversion.

clue.text: Dessert gets better, when on mountain peak

parts.note: an ice is a frozen dessert
to cap is to better or outdo

explanation.surface: A pudding improves when eaten up on a summit.
explanation.definitionFit: An icecap is a permanent covering of ice, found on a mountain summit.

clue.text: Heart must have died — once more — within a mile

indicators.note: the doubled letter sits within the distance

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: once more means the letter is given a second time

explanation.surface: Someone's heart gave out repeatedly within a mile of running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once more' gives the D for died a second time, and 'within' places the pair inside the distance.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart of something is its middle or centre.

clue.text: Brown paper that an animal will twist

indicators.note: the letters of the creature's name are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: An animal will rip through a sheet of brown wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: Manila is a strong brown paper used for envelopes and folders.

clue.text: A drab green cloak found in a rowdy spot

indicators.note: to cloak is to disguise, so the letters appear in a disguised order

explanation.surface: A dull green coat turns up in a noisy place.
explanation.definitionFit: A bear garden was a place for bear-baiting, so the term means any scene of rowdy disorder.

clue.text: This uniform, quite different it is not

definitions.meaning: the opposite of quite different, that is identical

explanation.definitionFit: The word means unchanging or identical, matching both uniform and not different.

clue.text: Utters a dictum, so there's nothing missed

indicators.note: missed means the letter for nothing is left out

parts.note: a say-so is an authoritative pronouncement or dictum
o, shaped like zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Someone pronounces a ruling, insisting nothing has been overlooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Says and utters are synonyms for speaks aloud.

clue.text: Curved fruit with a humiliating skin?

definitions.meaning: its skin is the classic thing to slip on, an embarrassing fall

explanation.definitionFit: The fruit is curved, and slipping on its skin is the stock humiliation of comedy.

clue.text: Meeting a circle, when a friend comes in

indicators.note: comes in means the friend goes inside the circle

parts.note: a ring is a circle
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A gathering forms a circle when a friend arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: A rallying is a coming together, a gathering or meeting of supporters.
